column1: # Game profile of Cult of the Lamb (Switch, update 1.5.28 = v1966080). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file
# Unity 2022.3.62f3 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 19.3.14; subsdk0 is the movie module (the Devolver logo and the intro movies are MP4s in StreamingAssets).
# The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles, read by unityfs.py (53,548), and the player's 11 GLSLC outputs in main.
# The game asks for present interval 1 and runs at 60 fps

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as one address
# region (main+0xb7e45c) and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The node area cut for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) shrinks the AddressRegionManager's node area to 62 MB.
# The layout of Ace Attorney Investigations Collection and Monster Train 2: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region).
# With the hardware pool (3.2 GB) StandardAllocator's 3.14 GB region left Unity's own regions about 1.2 GB: the alias region reached +4.25 GB 25 s after boot, the title drew only its
# clear colour, and the first movie crashed in Unity's ALLOC_DEFAULT_THREAD allocator (a write at NULL + 0xffffe0, main+0x6f86ec). With 1 GB: +3.51 GB in the first fight, 1.75 GB mapped
# The game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode(near = 0), so its vertex shaders use the main0_z entries; the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles
